Bird Chaser

🌅 Twitches today

    📍 Closest patches

    Recent species in your region that aren't on your eBird list yet.

      🎯 Open targets

        🏞 Stake out a hotspot

          Pick a place and see what eBird's hotspot page buries: who actually birds it, what it holds that nowhere else does, and which of its birds you still need.

          🔎 Stakeout bird

              Look up ANY bird — including ones already on your year list — and see every place it has been reported in range, with the checklist, count, date and distance behind each one.

                🌳 Spuh finder

                Browse uncertain bird IDs from broad to specific. The taxonomy is fetched directly from eBird once, then its compact model is cached on this device.

                  🧭 Look up a place

                  A temporary home. Fetches what is actually being reported around somewhere else — 3 calls, whatever the distance — so you can see a county your report never covers. One slot: scouting somewhere new replaces it, and your own report is never touched.

                  📆 Due back soon

                  Every species ever recorded in the region, checked against seven years of GBIF history for when it usually returns — so you know what to expect before it turns up. The first run reads hundreds of records and can be stopped and resumed; after that it is instant.

                    🥇 Today’s patches

                    Hotspots with the most species you still need, ranked by score (rarities ×3).

                      🚗 Half-day patches

                      Target-rich hotspots for a half-day outing, with county scope derived from Home.

                        🛣️ Full-day patches

                        Farther target-rich hotspots worth planning a full day around, loaded only when this section opens.

                          🧭 Trip planner

                          A nearest-neighbour route through your best nearby target hotspots.

                            🦜 Big days

                            Recent regional checklists ranked by species count.

                              🚶 Find local patches

                              The richest eBird hotspots within ~20 mi of Home (needs Home set).

                                🔖 Favorite patches

                                  Search above, or save hotspots from the other lists to pin them here.

                                    ❓ Needs proof

                                      Your tentative IDs awaiting a confirmation sighting. These are held OFF your year list everywhere in the app, so they keep showing up as targets until you drop them.

                                        🔔 Bird Gen

                                        🌤 Twitch weather

                                        Sun, moon, tides, and the NOAA forecast for your Home location.

                                        🌙 BirdCast

                                        🚨 Twitches this week

                                        Every rare species currently being reported — one row per species, closest report first.

                                          📅 My year

                                          Import your eBird CSV in Settings to see your totals.

                                            🏆 Top 100

                                            Your standing plus the full Top 100 board for the region you’re birding, and how your rank has moved since you started tracking. Switch regions from the nav, or pick a county board here.

                                            🧭 Pro patches

                                            Where the hundred busiest birders in these counties actually spend their effort — ranked by how disproportionately they choose a place, not by how many checklists it holds.

                                            🔭 Fresh ticks

                                            The newest species each top-100 birder added this year, grouped by bird — several birders sharing one tick means it is reliably gettable right now.

                                              🦅 Mega rarities

                                              Continent-wide megararities from eBird's ABA alert, flagged against your seen list.

                                                🌄 Dawn and dusk

                                                Finds dawn-only and dusk/night species from recent checklist times — grows richer each time you sample.

                                                🥚 Nemesis birds

                                                ⭐ Iconic spots near me

                                                Which places near you are unusually good for a particular bird — the signal eBird calls Iconic Birds. Needs your Home location.

                                                🔥 Hot patches

                                                Ranks nearby hotspots running hot — fresh sightings surging right now. Needs your Home location.

                                                🥶 Cold patches

                                                Overlooked gems — high all-time diversity hotspots that are currently quiet. Needs your Home location.

                                                👥 Convoys

                                                Detects birding groups (2+ people sharing 2+ hotspots in a day) from recent checklists — their route is a tested itinerary worth copying.

                                                🛬 On passage

                                                First reports load automatically from eBird when you open this section.
                                                County history predicts which species should arrive or depart in the next 2 weeks. The one-time build is resumable.

                                                🏅 Break a record

                                                Megararities that are DUE here — rare enough to be a record, and not found yet this year.

                                                📘 How each section works

                                                Every section, what it reads, how it decides, and what it cannot tell you.

                                                ⚙️ Settings

                                                Scales every label, list and bird photo in the app. Applies immediately — no need to save.

                                                Adds the Latin name to the bigger bird cards, in italics — Setophaga nigrescens under Black-throated Gray Warbler. The compact lists stay as they are.

                                                System follows your phone. An explicit choice wins until you set it back — picking Light keeps the app light even when the phone is dark. Easy read below is a separate switch and works with any of the three.

                                                Bigger tap targets, more space between things, stronger contrast, underlined links and a focus ring you can see. Works with the text size above rather than replacing it — if you are on Huge, you stay on Huge.

                                                Every “Open in Maps” link and the trip route open here. Applies immediately. OpenStreetMap directions take only a start and an end, so a multi-stop route says so instead of quietly dropping the stops in between.

                                                Switching happens when you press Save, and reloads the app. Each profile keeps a separate eBird key, alert code, year list, favourites and rank history, so several accounts can be tested on one phone. Hotspot, GBIF and taxonomy caches are shared on purpose — they describe places, not you, and re-fetching them per profile would burn the API budget you are trying to test.

                                                Get a key opens eBird's key request form. Sign in with your eBird account, submit the short form, then copy the key it shows you and tap Paste. It is free, issued instantly, and stored only on this device — it is never sent anywhere but eBird.

                                                Pick which birding report to chase. Every section below matches that report's counties, home base, and seen-species list exactly.

                                                Add your own region for a trip and chase from wherever you're staying. Type a name and the place you'll sleep — the coordinate, region code and time zone are worked out from it. A new region starts with an empty seen list, which on a trip is very nearly true, so every bird counts as one you still need.

                                                eBird region for the selected report (set automatically). Rankings/alerts use this scope.

                                                Used to find your row on eBird leaderboards. It's the public name on your eBird profile.

                                                eBird alert id for the “ABA Rarities” needs alert (default SN10489). Paste a regional RBA alert id to track a smaller area.

                                                Rankings and the ABA alert need an eBird login. The in-app browser keeps you signed in on this device until you sign out.

                                                Type a city, address, or waypoint (or paste “lat, lng”) and tap Find to fill in the coordinates below.

                                                Adds distances and a home marker to Top destinations. Also drives the Conditions forecast (US only).

                                                For coastal tides in Conditions. Find yours at tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov. Leave blank inland.

                                                No seen list yet. eBird → Download My Data → import MyEBirdData.csv.

                                                Asks eBird for your life list the way the app would (F8). If this works, the app can stop depending on hand-exported lists.

                                                Four features (F2, F8, F11, F19) are parked behind eBird's bot wall. It is a JavaScript puzzle, so a real browser view solves it automatically — this opens one, then checks whether the app's own requests get through afterwards. Tap it, wait for the page to finish, then close it.

                                                Removes your API key, seen list, favourites, home locations and every cached panel from this device. Nothing was ever sent anywhere else, so this is the whole of it.
